# Best portable power stations for a CPAP

These sites mostly do research from spec sheets rather than hands-on testing, and they disagree on some numbers. The picks below hold up across several of them.

## My picks

**Best overall: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (~$700)**
- It has 1,024 Wh of capacity, a very low noise rating (about 20 dB under 200 W) and a 10 ms UPS switchover, so it keeps running if the power cuts while you sleep.
- It recharges in about 49 minutes.
- Expect about 2.7 nights with the humidifier off and 1.2 to 1.7 nights with it on.
- Sources: [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/) and [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/), which has Amazon and official-store links.

**Best value: Bluetti AC180 (1,152 Wh, about $449 to $499)**
- It has the most capacity per dollar of the mainstream picks, at about 3.1 nights humidifier-off and 1.4 nights humidifier-on ([BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)).
- Its UPS switchover is 20 ms, slower than the Anker's.
- It's heavy at about 35 lb. One guide lists 16.5 lb, but that appears to be a kg/lb mix-up, since Bluetti's spec is ~16 kg.
- Buy: [Bluetti AC180 at Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180), which lists $499 and a code (AFF5OFF) that takes $24.95 off. It's an affiliate link to Bluetti's official store.

**Best if you want whole-home backup: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus (~$719)**
- Its capacity and UPS speed match the Anker, and it can expand to 5 kWh, which is roughly 8 humidifier-on nights ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)).
- It's the heaviest of the group at about 27 lb.
- Prices and purchase links: [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/).

**Small and cheap: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus (~$279 to $299)**
- At 10.4 lb it's easy to carry, but 286 Wh covers only about 0.8 of a night with the humidifier off and less than a night with it on.
- One guide claims it covers a "multi-night" CPAP-only load ([Outage Power Guide](https://outagepowerguide.com/reviews/best-power-station-for-cpap-machines/)). That doesn't match the math, since 286 Wh against roughly 320 Wh per night comes up short. I'd trust the other sources.
- It can expand to 858 Wh with an extra battery. Check prices at [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/).

## Worth knowing
- **Humidifier:** a heated humidifier roughly doubles power draw. If you use one, buy about 1,000 Wh or more.
- **Sizing:** nightly Wh × nights ÷ 0.85. For two humidifier-on nights that's about 1,200 Wh, so the 1,000 Wh class gives you a bit under two nights. Turning off the humidifier and heated tube stretches a charge the most.
- **DC cord:** using your CPAP maker's 12V DC cord can add roughly 10 to 20% runtime ([BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)). Don't use a generic car adapter.
- **Jackery caution:** Jackery says its power stations aren't recommended for medical devices, and the Explorer 1000 v2's UPS switchover is slower (up to 20 ms). I'd skip it for CPAP unless your device maker okays it ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)).
- **Prices vary by site,** so check the retailer at checkout.

This is general buying guidance, not medical advice. If you depend on CPAP therapy, check your machine's wattage label and talk to your provider or equipment supplier about a backup plan.

If you tell me your CPAP model, whether you use the humidifier, and how many nights of backup you want, I can narrow this to one pick.
